data:
Configuring, deploying, testing and releasing.
Configuration Deployment Testing and linting Versioning and releases

data.configuration#Configuration:
All configuration is environment variables in one root file, read by Docker Compose, the Python apps (load_dotenv()) and the Vite frontends (envDir):
$ cp .env.example .env .env.example is the full, commented list, set up for local dev. Under Docker Compose, docker-compose.yml sets the networking variables (hosts, ports, MinIO endpoint, API URL).
Variable Default Used by Description SIM_OPS_NG_SCENARIO data/demo.json sim Scenario loaded at start. See scenarios.md. SIM_OPS_NG_SOCKET_HOST 127.0.0.1 sim, api Engine socket bind host / host the API connects to (sim-ops-ng-sim in compose). SIM_OPS_NG_SOCKET_PORT 5555 sim, api Engine socket port. SIM_OPS_NG_API_HOST 0.0.0.0 api API bind host. SIM_OPS_NG_API_PORT 9111 api API port. SIM_OPS_NG_API_URL http://localhost:9111 admin Where the admin app reaches the API. SIM_OPS_NG_ADMIN_HOST / _PORT / _WORKERS 0.0.0.0 / 9131 / 4 admin gunicorn bind and workers. SIM_OPS_NG_ADMIN_PASSWORD admin123 api, admin Instructor password. SIM_OPS_NG_USER_PASSWORD user123 api Operator password (changeable at runtime). FLASK_SECRET_KEY random admin Signs the admin session cookie. If unset, admin logins end when the admin app restarts. SIM_OPS_NG_MINIO_ENDPOINT localhost:9000 sim, api Object store (sim-ops-ng-minio:9000 in compose). SIM_OPS_NG_MINIO_ROOT_USER / _PASSWORD myusername / mypassword sim, api, minio Object store credentials. VITE_CESIUM_TOKEN — 3dv (build) Cesium Ion token. VITE_SO_API, VITE_WS_URL same origin mcs (dev only) API and WebSocket URLs for npm run dev. The nginx build forces them empty. SIM_OPS_NG_WS_URL derived admin WebSocket URL the admin page connects to. The default passwords are for local use only: change them, and set FLASK_SECRET_KEY, before exposing the stack to a network.

data.1-services#1. Services:
Service Image Exposed Notes sim-ops-ng-minio Dockerfile.minio 9001 (console) Object store for packets and products; data in the minio-data volume. sim-ops-ng-sim Dockerfile.lib — Engine; binds its socket on 0.0.0.0 inside the network. sim-ops-ng-api Dockerfile.lib — API. sim-ops-ng-admin Dockerfile.lib — Admin panel. sim-ops-ng-3dv Dockerfile.3dv — 3D viewer; VITE_CESIUM_TOKEN is a build argument. sim-ops-ng-nginx Dockerfile.nginx 8080 Builds the MCS and serves it, and proxies everything else. Only nginx (8080) and the MinIO console (9001, on 127.0.0.1 only) are published; everything else is reached on the internal sim-ops-net network.
One Python image. sim, api and admin share the sim-ops-ng-lib image (uv, from uv.lock, with de421.bsp baked in) and differ only in command. MinIO is built from source (no upstream images; MINIO_RELEASE pins it). The Go build needs ~2 GB: on a small Docker VM build it alone first (docker compose build sim-ops-ng-minio). Healthchecks gate startup: minio → sim → api → admin/3dv → nginx. Non-root. The Python services run as simops (uid 1000), MinIO as minio (uid 1000), and nginx/3dv use nginx-unprivileged (uid 101, listening on 8080 inside the container).
data.2-nginx#2. nginx: containers/nginx/nginx.conf is the main config; routing is in architecture.md. containers/nginx/3dv.conf serves the 3dv container.
data.deployment#Deployment:
Docker Compose (docker-compose.yml), images from containers/, build context the repo root.
$ docker compose build $ docker compose up -d

data.1-one-version#1. One version:
The root VERSION file is the source of truth, mirrored in sim-ops-ng-lib/pyproject.toml, so/__init__.py and the MCS and 3DV package.json. Change it only with bin/version.sh:
$ sh bin/version.sh # print the current version $ sh bin/version.sh check # verify every component matches VERSION (CI runs this) $ sh bin/version.sh set 0.1.0 # bump everything, and refresh the lock files It is served at /api/version; the MCS and 3DV bake it in at build time (__APP_VERSION__).
data.2-cutting-a-release#2. Cutting a release: Move the ## Unreleased notes in CHANGELOG.md under a new ## X.Y.Z - YYYY-MM-DD heading. sh bin/version.sh set X.Y.Z, then commit. git tag X.Y.Z && git push origin X.Y.Z — plain X.Y.Z, no v prefix. The tag runs release.yml: after the lib, mcs, 3dv and docker workflows pass, bin/release.sh builds dist/sim-ops-ng-X.Y.Z.zip (a git archive of the tag minus .gitattributes export-ignore paths) and a GitHub release is published with the changelog section as notes (missing section = failure). Build the zip locally with sh bin/release.sh X.Y.Z.

data.1-backend#1. Backend: $ cd sim-ops-ng-lib $ uv run pytest -v $ sh bin/lint.sh # pylint: so, bin and tests Tests live in sim-ops-ng-lib/tests/.
data.2-frontends#2. Frontends: $ cd sim-ops-ng-mcs $ npm run lint # ESLint, with --fix $ npm run typecheck # vue-tsc -b $ npm run test:unit # Vitest, tests in src/**/__tests__/ $ npm run build # type check + production build $ cd sim-ops-ng-3dv $ npm run lint $ npm test # Vitest, tests in src/__tests__/ $ npm run build # tsc + production build
data.3-ci#3. CI:
GitHub Actions in .github/workflows/, each triggered by its own paths; every step blocks.
Workflow Runs sim-ops-ng-lib-test-and-lint.yml uv sync --locked, bin/lint.sh (pylint over so, bin and tests), pytest -v sim-ops-ng-mcs-lint-and-build.yml npm ci, eslint, npm run typecheck, npm run test:unit, vite build sim-ops-ng-3dv-lint-and-build.yml npm ci, eslint, npm test, npm run build (tsc + vite build) docker.yml docker compose build, then up --wait (every healthcheck must pass) and a smoke test through nginx; on any change outside docs/ and *.md version-check.yml sh bin/version.sh check release.yml On a tag: runs the lib, mcs, 3dv and docker workflows first, see releasing.md. docs.yml Builds these docs (Hugo, pinned) and publishes them to GitHub Pages.
data.4-the-docs#4. The docs:
Plain markdown in docs/; docs/site/ builds a Hugo site with the Hextra theme (submodule at docs/site/themes/hextra):
$ git submodule update --init $ hugo server --config docs/site/hugo.toml # from the repo root A new page needs title/weight front matter and its filename added to one of the mounts in docs/site/hugo.toml.

data:
What talks to the simulator: the REST/WebSocket API, the operators’ MCS, the 3D viewer and the instructor’s admin panel.
REST and WebSocket API MCS — Monitoring and Control System 3DV — 3D visualization Admin panel

data.1-data#1. Data: Reads the password-less, read-only /api/ws/viewer WebSocket. It ignores link state, so the orbit moves without FRAME_LOCK. Draws the current breakpoint’s ground station; reconnects with a 1 s → 15 s back-off.
data.2-what-it-shows#2. What it shows: The spacecraft — bus, solar panels, antenna — oriented along its pointing target (Sun or nadir). The ground station dish. Uplink and downlink as animated “wave” lines between them, following the link state.
data.3-build#3. Build: $ cd sim-ops-ng-3dv $ npm install $ npm run dev $ npm run build $ npm run lint VITE_CESIUM_TOKEN (Cesium Ion) is baked in at build time; Docker passes it from .env as a build argument.
data.3dv--3d-visualization#3DV — 3D visualiza: A CesiumJS view of the spacecraft in orbit and the ground station, in sim-ops-ng-3dv/: the scene in src/main.ts, with unit-tested helpers in src/geometry.ts and src/format.ts. Served at /3dv/ behind nginx.

data.1-session-control#1. Session control:
Log in with SIM_OPS_NG_ADMIN_PASSWORD, then:
Start / stop / pause / resume the simulation. Stopping resets everything (sim_loop.md). Next / previous breakpoint — move between passes. Load a scenario from data/. Data proxy — SLE (telemetry only at FRAME_LOCK) or EGSE (always). Change the user password — disconnects every operator. Set spacecraft state (/api/admin/set-state), bypassing the bus and link checks; only the fields in SimOps._do_admin_set_state() (modes, antennas, TX/RX status, MCU, OBSW mode, memory, battery DoD, ACU, PDU). Trigger safe mode — the on-board FDIR action, link-independent.
data.2-overrides#2. Overrides:
Overrides force a value after each step, so they always win until unset.
Kind Attributes Ground station status_dl, max_status_dl, max_c_no_dl, max_eb_no_dl, frame_quality, no_tm, no_tc Spacecraft any scalar (number, boolean, text) or enum SpacecraftState field, e.g. aocs_valid, eps_battery_dod; eps_sol_array takes one value for both arrays. Other list fields (aocs_rotation, pl_gnss_pos, the DHS windows, …) can’t be overridden. Enum values are given by name. no_tm stops telemetry outright; no_tc rejects every command.
data.3-triggers#3. Triggers:
Triggers are scripted failures: data/trigger-.py, run as a subprocess (60 s timeout) by the admin app’s POST /api/trigger/ (/admin/api/trigger/ behind nginx). Each is a list of steps, routed by run_control_steps() in so/utils.py:
Step system Goes to override /api/override/set (or /unset with control: "_unset") any, with admin: true /api/admin/set-state spacecraft, ground_station /api/control What each trigger does is exercise content: read the script, don’t document it here. To add one, drop a script in data/ and register it in TRIGGER_SCRIPTS in so/admin.py.
data.admin-panel#Admin panel: The instructor’s panel: a Flask app (so/admin.py, templates in so/templates/) under gunicorn on :9131 (/admin/ behind nginx). It is an API client using the admin password.

data.1-authentication#1. Authentication:
Two shared passwords, from the environment:
Role Variable Passed as User (operators) SIM_OPS_NG_USER_PASSWORD header X-User-Password Admin (instructor) SIM_OPS_NG_ADMIN_PASSWORD header X-Admin-Password Never in query strings (they would end up in access logs). Browsers can’t set WebSocket headers, so WebSocket clients offer two subprotocols, sim-ops and sim-ops.password.; the server selects sim-ops:
const b64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new TextEncoder().encode(password))) .replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, ''); new WebSocket(url, ['sim-ops', `sim-ops.password.${b64}`]); Changing the user password closes open user WebSockets (code 1008).
data.2-endpoints#2. Endpoints:
Open
Method Path Returns GET /api/version {version} GET /api/sim Version, running flag, scenario, breakpoint, data proxy, sle_connected. GET /api/scenario The loaded scenario. Without the admin password (and on the user WebSocket), breakpoints come without sc_initial_state / gs_initial_state: they may set up a planned fault.
User (X-User-Password; the admin password is accepted too, except on /api/auth)
Method Path Does GET /api/auth 200 if the password is right, else 401. GET /api/state Last spacecraft (operator view) and ground_station state. POST /api/control {system, control, value} → {status}; 400 if the command never ran (sim stopped, timed out, bad value). Operators may only control the ground_station; spacecraft controls need the admin password. See commanding.md. GET /api/obj-store/tm TM/TC buckets and their objects. GET /api/obj-store/fd Flight-dynamics products. GET /api/obj-store/sp/{bucket}/{object} One decoded space packet. POST /api/tc-stack Push {command, system, control, value} (max 5). Only spacecraft TCs from the operator catalogue (OPERATOR_TC_CONTROLS in so/api.py), else 403. DELETE /api/tc-stack/{index} Remove an entry; 400 if there is none at that index. POST /api/tc-stack/execute Execute the head of the stack → {status, command}. POST /api/tc-stack/send Execute the given TC right away, bypassing the stack (file uploads) → {status, command}. Admin (X-Admin-Password)
Method Path Does POST /api/start Start the loop at the first breakpoint (409 if already running). POST /api/stop, /api/pause, /api/resume Loop lifecycle (sim_loop.md). POST /api/next-breakpoint[?restart=true], /api/previous-breakpoint Move between breakpoints; returns the new breakpoint, 400 if there is none. GET /api/scenarios *.json files in data/. POST /api/scenario/load {filename} — load a scenario from data/. GET /api/overrides Active overrides. POST /api/override/set, /api/override/unset {attr, value} — see admin.md. POST /api/admin/set-state {attr, value} — set a spacecraft field directly, bypassing commanding. POST /api/data-proxy {mode: "SLE" | "EGSE"}. GET / POST /api/admin/user-password Read / change the user password.
data.3-websockets#3. WebSockets: Path Auth Receives /api/ws user password (subprotocol) The state broadcast, with spacecraft filtered by the data proxy. /api/ws/admin admin password (subprotocol) The full broadcast, with the unfiltered spacecraft state as spacecraft, whatever the link state. /api/ws/viewer none Read-only subset for the 3D view: spacecraft position/attitude (unfiltered), ground-station link and pass state, and the current breakpoint. A wrong password closes the socket with code 1008. Each socket gets the latest state on connect, then every broadcast (contents). bin/ws-client.py is a small debug listener.
data.rest-and-websocket-api#REST and WebSocke: SimOpsAPI in so/api.py: FastAPI on :9111, at /api behind nginx. Commands go to the engine over the socket link (architecture.md); state reads come from the last broadcast.

data.1-data-flow#1. Data flow: Reads from the user WebSocket (/api/ws), commands over REST (api.md). In SLE mode telemetry only arrives at downlink FRAME_LOCK; otherwise displays go stale and Last Update shows their age. A dropped socket reconnects (1 s → 15 s back-off) behind a banner.
data.2-stores#2. Stores: Store File Holds Socket app-websockets.ts The WebSocket, its connection status and reconnects, and the latest sc_state, gs_state, sim_ts, tc_stack, tc_history, data_proxy and sle_connected. Auth app-auth.ts The user password, in sessionStorage (per tab). A rejected password (socket closed with 1008, or /api/auth failing) re-prompts. Options app-option.ts App options, including the API base URL (VITE_SO_API, empty = same origin).
data.3-views#3. Views:
Routes are in src/router/; views in src/views/.
Route View Purpose / Dashboard.vue Overview. /aocs, /ttc, /eps, /dhs, /payload per subsystem Subsystem telemetry. /spacecraft Spacecraft.vue Spacecraft overview. /ground_station GroundStation.vue Station state, lock status, spectra (GroundStationPanel.vue). /gs_config GSConfig.vue Ground-station configuration. /spacon SpaCon.vue Spacecraft controller: build and execute the TC stack. /om OM.vue The same panel plus ground-station control: uplink carrier, sweep, power, bands, tracking. /commands Commands.vue The command catalogue. /procedures Procedures.vue Operational procedures. /flight-dynamics FlightDynamics.vue Flight-dynamics products. /packet-store PacketStore.vue Stored TM/TC space packets. /history History.vue The last TCs executed from the shared stack, with their acknowledgement. /about About.vue
data.4-development#4. Development:
$ cd sim-ops-ng-mcs $ npm install $ npm run dev # Vite dev server $ npm run build # type check + production build Lint and tests: testing.md. The dev server needs VITE_SO_API and VITE_WS_URL in the root .env.
Shared pieces live in src/components/app/: TelemetryStatus (the WS and D/L header badges), LastUpdate (the telemetry footer), ConnectionBanner, AckStatus (a g:REL g:ACC g:EXE acknowledgement) and GroundStationPanel.
Every
data.mcs--monitoring-and-control-system#MCS —: The operators’ frontend: Vue 3 + TypeScript, Pinia stores and Vue Router, in sim-ops-ng-mcs/. Served at / behind nginx.

data.1-configure#1. Configure: $ cp .env.example .env Defaults work locally; read configuration.md before exposing the stack.
data.2-run-with-docker#2. Run with Docker: $ docker compose build $ docker compose up -d URL What Password http://localhost:8080 MCS SIM_OPS_NG_USER_PASSWORD (default user123) http://localhost:8080/admin Admin panel SIM_OPS_NG_ADMIN_PASSWORD (default admin123) http://localhost:8080/3dv 3D viewer — The simulation starts stopped: start it from the admin panel. The first build compiles MinIO from source (a few minutes, ~2 GB of memory).
data.3-run-manually#3. Run manually:
.env.example already points everything at localhost. One terminal per service:
$ cd sim-ops-ng-lib $ export PYTHONPATH=. $ uv run bin/sim-ops.py # sim engine, socket on :5555 $ uv run bin/sim-ops-api.py # REST/WebSocket API on :9111 $ uv run bin/admin.py # admin panel on :9131 $ sh bin/run-devel.sh # ...or all three in one screen session On first use skyfield downloads de421.bsp (~17 MB) into sim-ops-ng-lib/. MinIO is optional: without it, packets and flight-dynamics products aren’t stored.
MCS (set VITE_SO_API and VITE_WS_URL in .env):
$ cd sim-ops-ng-mcs $ npm install $ npm run dev
data.4-a-first-pass#4. A first pass: In the admin panel, Start the simulation. The first breakpoint loads. In the MCS OM view, wait for the spacecraft to rise above 5°, switch the uplink carrier on and run a sweep. Once the downlink reaches FRAME_LOCK, telemetry appears and commands can be sent from SpaCon. See commanding.md for the acknowledgements.

data:
The engine: processes, the tick, scenarios and breakpoints, commanding, and the RF link.
Architecture The simulation loop Scenarios and breakpoints Commanding Ground station RF link budget

data.1-processes#1. Processes: Process Entry point Port Role Sim engine bin/sim-ops.py → SimOps :5555 (TCP) Runs the simulation loop and owns all state. API bin/sim-ops-api.py → SimOpsAPI :9111 (HTTP/WS) Authenticates clients, forwards commands to the engine, relays state broadcasts to WebSockets. Admin bin/admin.py → Flask under gunicorn :9131 (HTTP) Instructor panel; a client of the API. MinIO built from source (Dockerfile.minio) :9000, console :9001 Object store for TM/TC space packets and flight-dynamics products. nginx containers/nginx/nginx.conf :8080 Serves the MCS and proxies everything else. The engine holds no passwords: authentication lives entirely in the API layer.
data.2-engine--api-the-socket-link#2. Engine:
JSON over TCP (so/communication.py): SocketServer in the engine, SocketClient in the API (reconnects if the engine restarts):
{"type": "command", "id": "…", "command": "control", "params": {"system": "spacecraft", "control": "aocs_mode", "value": "SUN"}} {"type": "response", "id": "…", "command": "control", "success": true, "data": {"status": "g:REL g:ACC g:EXE"}} After {"type": "subscribe"} a client gets a snapshot, then a "type": "state" broadcast every tick. Handlers are registered in SimOps._setup_socket_handlers(); those that mutate state run in the sim thread via a queue (sim_loop.md).
data.3-the-state-broadcast#3. The state broad:
Each broadcast (SimOps._broadcast_state()) carries:
Key Content ts Simulated timestamp (epoch seconds). running, paused Loop status. data_proxy, sle_connected SLE or EGSE, and whether spacecraft TM is currently delivered. scenario, breakpoint The loaded scenario and active breakpoint. spacecraft The SpacecraftState as operators see it — null when there is no telemetry. spacecraft_admin The full, unfiltered SpacecraftState. ground_station The GroundStationState. tc_stack, tc_history The shared telecommand stack and the last ten executions. Enum fields are serialised by name (custom_dict_factory in so/data_model.py).
Data proxy. SLE (default): spacecraft is null unless the downlink is at FRAME_LOCK. EGSE: always delivered, as on the bench. With the TTC MCU in error, spacecraft is scrubbed (SpacecraftState.scrub()). Per-WebSocket relaying: api.md.
data.4-object-store#4. Object store:
When MinIO is reachable (SIM_OPS_NG_MINIO_*), the engine stores:
TM packets — a CCSDS space packet of the spacecraft state every tm_packet_frequency simulated seconds, in sim--tm (in SLE mode only at FRAME_LOCK). TC packets — every command released to the spacecraft (g:REL), in sim--tc. Flight-dynamics products — the pass’s tracking data at its end (SLE mode only), in flight-dynamics. See ground_station.md. Packets are built by SpacePacketHandler (so/utils.py). Without MinIO the engine logs a warning and carries on.
data.5-nginx-routing#5. nginx routing: Path Upstream / The built MCS (static). /api/, /api/ws sim-ops-ng-api:9111 /admin/ sim-ops-ng-admin:9131 /3dv/ sim-ops-ng-3dv:8080
data.architecture#Architecture: The processes and what crosses between them. Per-tick engine internals: sim_loop.md.

data.1-the-path-of-a-command#1. The path of a:
MCS SpaCon ──▶ POST /api/tc-stack (push, max 5 entries, shared by all operators) ──▶ POST /api/tc-stack/execute (run the head of the stack, FIFO) ──▶ POST /api/tc-stack/send (file uploads: run the given TC) │ SimOps._do_control() ──▶ SpacecraftSim.control() ──▶ CommunicationBus.send() │ .command(state, BusMessage) A stack entry is {command, system, control, value}, e.g. TC_AOCS_001 setting aocs_mode = SUN. Operators can only push catalogue TCs; controls that set internal state (e.g. eps_battery_dod, trigger_safe_mode) are admin-only, via /api/control.
The control name’s prefix picks the subsystem (aocs_, ttc_, eps_, dhs_, pl_); trigger_safe_mode goes to the DHS. Every command is logged in the DHS TC history.
data.2-acknowledgement-format#2. Acknowledgem:
{rel}:REL {acc}:ACC {exe}:EXE — release (ground), acceptance and execution (on board), each prefixed with:
Prefix Meaning g Green — confirmed OK. w Warning (reserved; not currently produced). r Red — failed. u Unknown — no telemetry to confirm the outcome either way. g:REL g:ACC g:EXE is full success. u is not a failure: the command may have executed, there is just no TM to prove it (e.g. no downlink frame lock).
data.3-high-priority-commands-hptc#3. High-pr: The only commands processed while the TTC MCU is in error (HPTC in so/core.py): all TC_TTC_*, the EPS power cycles TC_EPS_041–044 and the TTC TX/RX power switches TC_EPS_051–058. Marked (hp) in the MCS catalogue.
data.4-catalogue-and-ground-station-controls#: The catalogue lives in the MCS (Commands.vue, SpaCon.vue); effects are on each subsystem page. Ground-station controls go straight to the ground station and answer OK or FAIL (ground_station.md).
data.commanding#Commanding: How a TC gets from the MCS to a subsystem and how to read the acknowledgement. Code: SimOps._do_control() in so/core.py, SpacecraftSim.control() and CommunicationBus in so/spacecraft.py.

data.1-passes-and-tracking#1. Passes and trac: On construction, skyfield finds the day’s passes over the station at 0° and 5° (next_pass_*, next_5_*). With program track on, each tick in a pass computes elevation, azimuth, range and range-rate (doppler_velocity); otherwise they are None and there is no link.
data.2-lock-states#2. Lock states:
Downlink status_dl and uplink ttc_state_ul both climb the TTCState ladder NO_RF → RF_DETECTED → PLL_LOCK → PSK_LOCK → BIT_LOCK → FRAME_LOCK by link margin; the thresholds are in rf_link.md. The uplink only locks after a sweep. A ground/spacecraft mode mismatch gives downlink NO_RF, though the spectrum still shows the signal. In SLE mode telemetry needs downlink FRAME_LOCK; commands need carrier and sweep.
Housekeeping each tick (_update_wrap_up): the uplink carrier drops below 5°; below the horizon the uplink state, sweep and frame quality reset; Doppler compensation needs PLL lock both ways; the sweep is lost when the carrier goes off or the uplink margin falls to −1 dB or below.
data.3-flight-dynamics#3. Flight dynamics: With program track, a sample [x, y, z, range, range-rate] is recorded every 10 s. Range needs auto range and spacecraft ranging; range-rate needs Doppler and a coherent transponder. At pass end (or breakpoint change) the samples go to MinIO as one product, validity 0–2 by how many of the two were collected. They are not broadcast.
data.4-controls#4. Controls:
GroundStationSim.control() answers OK or FAIL:
Control Values Notes carrier_ul on / off on only at ≥ 5° elevation. sweep true / false Needs the carrier on. power_ul dBm, 0–70 Commands need ≥ 50. mode a TTCModes name Must match the spacecraft’s for downlink lock. band_ul S / X Not while the carrier is on; a change clears the sweep. program_track, auto_track, auto_range, doppler_enabled true / false frame_checks enabled / disabled
data.5-spectra#5. Spectra: SpectrumGenerator synthesises spectrum_ul / spectrum_dl from modulation, bandwidth, Eb/N0 and Doppler. The instructor can override downlink results (admin.md, rf_link.md).
data.ground-station#Ground station:
Pass prediction, antenna tracking, the downlink side of the RF link, lock states and spectra. Code: so/ground_station.py (GroundStationSim, SpectrumGenerator).
It computes the downlink budget (_calc_link_budget_dl); the TTC computes the uplink (ttc.md); both follow rf_link.md. band_ul is independent of the downlink mode (S up with X down is allowed).

data.1-the-equations#1. The equations:
All quantities in dB unless noted; evaluated for each direction every tick:
C/N0 = EIRP − L_fs − L_atm − L_pol − L_point + G/T − k [dBHz] Eb/N0 = C/N0 − L_mod − 10·log10(R_b) [dB] margin = Eb/N0 + G_coding − (Eb/N0)_req [dB] BER = ½ · erfc( √(10^(Eb/N0 / 10)) ) FER = 1 − (1 − BER)^8192 Symbol Meaning Where it comes from EIRP Effective isotropic radiated power, dBW §2 L_fs Free-space path loss §3.1 L_atm Atmospheric loss §3.2 L_pol Polarisation mismatch loss §3.3 L_point Ground antenna pointing loss §3.4 G/T Receiver figure of merit, dB/K §2 k Boltzmann’s constant, −228.6 dBW/K/Hz (10·log10(1.380649e−23)) BOLTZMANN_DBW L_mod Carrier modulation loss §4.4 R_b Bit rate, bit/s §4.1 G_coding Channel coding gain §4.4 (Eb/N0)_req Eb/N0 required for BER 1e−5 §4.4 Notes:
k is negative, so − k adds 228.6 dB. BER uses the uncoded Eb/N0: the coding gain only enters the margin. FER assumes an 8192-bit frame; BER is clamped to [0, 1] first.
data.2-terms-per-direction#2. Terms, per dire: Term Downlink (spacecraft → ground) Uplink (ground → spacecraft) Mode the spacecraft’s ttc_mode ul_mode(gs.mode, gs.band_ul): the ground station’s mode with its band letter replaced by band_ul (e.g. X_Sup_LBR with band_ul = S → S_Sup_LBR) Frequency f dl_freq_mhz of the mode ul_freq_mhz of the uplink mode Bit rate R_b dl_bit_rate_bps ul_bit_rate_bps Spacecraft antenna ttc_s_antenna if the band is S, ttc_x_antenna if X same, for the uplink band Transmit power P_sc = SC_TX_POWER_DBW[power_class] (3 or 7 dBW) power_ul (dBm, from the GS control, default 50) − 30 → dBW Transmit antenna gain G_sc = SC_ANTENNA_GAIN_DB[antenna] G_gs = dish gain at f (§3.5) EIRP P_sc + G_sc − L_tx (power_ul − 30) + G_gs − L_tx Receive G/T G_gs − T_gs = dish gain at f − 22 dBK G_sc − T_sc = antenna gain − 27 dBK Modulation, coding of the spacecraft’s mode of the uplink mode Elevation, range from the ground station’s tracking (elevation, distance in km) same L_tx is the transmitter line loss, 1 dB on both sides (TX_LOSS_DB). G_gs is computed separately at the uplink and downlink frequencies.
data.32-atmospheric-loss#3.2 Atmospheric loss:
A simplified ITU-R P.618 model: a zenith loss scaled by the cosecant of the elevation:
L_zenith = 0.3 + 0.1·f_GHz L_atm = L_zenith / sin(max(el, 5°)) Elevation is clamped at 5° (ATM_MIN_ELEVATION_DEG, also when missing or negative) so the loss is continuous across AOS. Maximum ≈ 6.02 dB at 2245 MHz, ≈ 13.1 dB at 8450 MHz.
data.33-polarisation-loss#3.3 Polarisation lo:
Keyed on the spacecraft antenna in use:
Antenna L_pol LGA_RHC, LGA_LHC 0.0 dB MGA 0.5 dB HGA 1.0 dB
data.34-pointing-loss#3.4 Pointing loss:
Ground antenna loss while autotrack settles near AOS:
el ≤ 0° → L_point = 5.0 0° < el < 2.6° → L_point = 5.0 · (1 − el / 2.6) el ≥ 2.6° → L_point = 0.0 (POINTING_LOSS_MAX_DB = 5.0, POINTING_LOSS_ELEVATION_DEG = 2.6.)
data.35-ground-dish-gain#3.5 Ground dish gain:
Parabolic dish of diameter D (m, the breakpoint’s antenna_diameter_m), aperture efficiency η = 0.55 (GS_ANTENNA_EFFICIENCY), c = 2.99792458e8 m/s:
G_gs = 10·log10(η) + 20·log10(π · D · f_Hz / c) [dBi] Example: D = 3.7 m → 36.20 dBi at 2245 MHz, 35.48 dBi at 2067 MHz.
data.36-doppler-shift#3.6 Doppler shift: Δf_MHz = (v_km/s · 1000 / c) · f_MHz v is the ground station’s doppler_velocity, positive when the spacecraft approaches.

data.5-no-link-conditions#5. No-link conditio:
A direction with no link reports C/N0, Eb/N0 and margin of −128.0 (NO_LINK_C_NO, NO_LINK_MARGIN), BER 0.5 (NO_LINK_BER), FER 1.0 (NO_LINK_FER) and no Doppler shift.
Downlink — no link if any of:
the spacecraft transmitter for the mode’s band (ttc_s_tx_status / ttc_x_tx_status) is not on; no elevation, or elevation < 0°; no range, or range < 0; the ground station’s mode band differs from the spacecraft’s; the band is X and the X antenna is HGA. Uplink — no link if any of:
no ground-station state; the uplink carrier (carrier_ul) is not on; no elevation, or elevation ≤ 0°; no range, or range ≤ 0. Elevation and range only exist during a pass with program track on (ground_station.md).
data.6-frequencies#6. Frequencies:
On board (TTC):
freq_rx = f_ul + Δf_ul freq_tx = freq_rx · TURNAROUND_RATIO[(band_ul, dl band)] if ttc_coherent = enabled = f_dl (nominal, of the spacecraft mode) otherwise On the ground: freq_ul_mhz is the nominal uplink frequency of the uplink mode, and
freq_dl = freq_tx + Δf_dl if coherent = f_dl + Δf_dl otherwise where Δf_ul and Δf_dl are the Doppler shifts (§3.6) at f_ul and f_dl.

Margin State > 3.0 dB FRAME_LOCK > 1.0 dB BIT_LOCK > −1.0 dB PLL_LOCK > −128 (any real signal) RF_DETECTED −128 (no link) NO_RF A mode mismatch between ground station and spacecraft forces the margin to −128 → NO_RF.
Uplink (ttc_state_ul), only if the spacecraft receiver for the uplink band is on and the ground station has swept:
Margin State > 2.0 dB BIT_LOCK > 0.0 dB PSK_LOCK > −1.0 dB PLL_LOCK otherwise NO_RF For carrier, sweep and Doppler housekeeping see ground_station.md.
data.8-instructor-overrides#8. Instructor ove:
Applied to the downlink after the budget, in order (admin.md):
max_c_no_dl caps C/N0; Eb/N0, margin, BER and FER are recomputed from it. max_eb_no_dl caps Eb/N0; margin, BER and FER are recomputed, and C/N0 back-computed as Eb/N0 + L_mod + 10·log10(R_b). max_status_dl caps the lock state.

data.rf-link-budget#RF link budget:
Both directions, from power and geometry to C/N0, Eb/N0, margin, BER, FER and lock state, enough to reproduce the numbers by hand. Code: so/rf_link.py, called by GroundStationSim._calc_link_budget_dl (downlink, so/ground_station.py) and TTCMin._calculate_uplink_budget (uplink, so/sys/ttc.py).
A Friis budget following CCSDS 401.0-B-32 (frequencies, bit rates, turnaround ratios) and CCSDS 131.0-B-5 (coding gains), with constants typical of a small LEO mission.

data.1-shipped-scenarios#1. Shipped scenarios: File Breakpoints Notes data/demo.json 4 Default (SIM_OPS_NG_SCENARIO). data/testing.json 4 time_factor: 0.5 (twice real time). The admin panel can load any *.json in data/ at runtime (POST /api/scenario/load); nothing outside data/ is accepted.
data.2-file-format#2. File format: { "name": "example", "tle": "SAT\n1 …\n2 …", "time_factor": 1.0, "tm_packet_frequency": 30, "breakpoints": [ { "name": "pass_1", "begin": "2030-01-01 10:00:00+00:00", "end": "2030-01-01 10:15:00+00:00", "ground_station": { "name": "GS-1", "latitude": 0.0, "longitude": 0.0, "altitude": 0, "antenna_diameter_m": 4.0 }, "gs_initial_state": { "carrier_ul": "off" }, "sc_initial_state": { } } ] } Field Default Meaning name — Scenario name; also names the MinIO buckets (sim--tm, sim--tc), so it must be 1–56 lowercase letters, digits, - or . (. not at either end, next to - or doubled; checked on load). tle — Three-line element set (name + two lines), used by AOCS and the ground station. Checked on load: two 69-character element lines starting 1 / 2 , same catalog number, valid checksums. time_factor 1.0 Wall-clock seconds per simulated second; a positive number. tm_packet_frequency 30 Seconds between stored TM packets; a positive integer. breakpoints[].name — Unique within the scenario (breakpoints are looked up by name). breakpoints[].begin / end — ISO timestamps of the window, with a timezone (+00:00 by convention; other offsets give the same instant); begin must be before end. A timestamp without a timezone fails the load. breakpoints[].ground_station — Station location and dish size (antenna_diameter_m, default 4.0). breakpoints[].gs_initial_state {} GroundStationState fields applied when the breakpoint starts. breakpoints[].sc_initial_state {} SpacecraftState fields applied when the breakpoint starts. Enum fields in initial states are given by name ("carrier_ul": "off"), lists element by element. A field the state doesn’t have, or an unknown enum name, fails the load (ValueError), as does an invalid or missing scenario or breakpoint field above (a malformed ground_station raises TypeError). The types of other initial-state values are not checked: a wrong one (e.g. "eps_battery_dod": "high") loads, then stops the simulation on that breakpoint’s first tick. Initial states are instructor-only: the API hides them from operators (api.md), so keep planned faults there and out of these docs.
data.3-breakpoints-at-runtime#3. Breakpoints:
When a breakpoint becomes active (step_loop, move_to_next_breakpoint, move_to_previous_breakpoint), the engine:
re-seeds the spacecraft’s time baseline to the breakpoint’s begin (see sim_loop.md); applies sc_initial_state and gs_initial_state over the current state (unlisted fields carry over); enforces the fixed invariants (apply_fixed_updates()); resets the flight-dynamics product flag and tracking samples for the new pass. next_breakpoint with restart=true wraps around to the first breakpoint.
data.scenarios-and-breakpoints#Scenarios and: A JSON file fixing the orbit and splitting the exercise into breakpoints, typically one per pass. Loader: load_scenario() in so/core.py; data classes in so/data_model.py.

data.1-real-time-environment#1. Real-time env:
The loop is a SimPy process running in a simpy.rt.RealtimeEnvironment on its own thread (SimOps._run_simops_thread()):
initial_time is the active breakpoint’s begin, so env.now is a UTC epoch timestamp. factor is the scenario’s time_factor: 1.0 is real time, 0.5 runs twice as fast. One tick advances time_step simulated seconds (default 1.0).
data.2-one-tick#2. One tick:
SimOps._simpy_process():
Drain the command queue — execute every pending command in the sim thread (§3). If paused, broadcast state and wait one tick without advancing simulated time. Compute ts = env.now + _ts_offset. GroundStationSim.update(ts, sc_state, gs_overrides) — geometry, downlink budget, lock state, spectra. See ground_station.md and rf_link.md. SpacecraftSim.update(ts, gs_state, sc_overrides) — the subsystem chain AOCS → TTC → EPS → DHS → Payload, then overrides. Broadcast the state (see architecture.md). Store a TM packet if int(ts) % tm_packet_frequency == 0, and try to write the pass’s flight-dynamics product. Sleep time_step (_sleep()), executing queued commands about every CMD_POLL_S (0.1 s) of wall time.
data.3-the-command-queue#3. The command queue:
The socket server runs each request on its own thread. Commands that change state (controls, TC execution, overrides, admin set-state, breakpoint moves) are queued instead (_send_cmd() → _command_queue) and run in the sim thread by _dispatch_cmd() within ~0.1 s, also between ticks.
The caller waits up to SEND_CMD_TIMEOUT (4 s, under the API’s 5 s, so the sim gives up first). A command whose caller timed out is cancelled and never runs. Stopping the loop fails anything still queued. Lifecycle and admin handlers (start/stop, breakpoints, overrides, scenario load) run one at a time (_admin_lock).
data.4-timestamps-and-deltas#4. Timestamps an: SpacecraftSim.update() sets _state.ts = ts only after the subsystems run, so they can use ts - _state.ts as the tick length (EPS battery, DHS memory). The baseline is seeded to the breakpoint’s begin (SpacecraftSim.__init__, and seed_ts() on each breakpoint change); otherwise the first delta would be measured from 0.0.
data.5-jumping-in-time#5. Jumping in time:
The effective timestamp is env.now + _ts_offset, so the clock can move without restarting SimPy:
Breakpoint change — the offset is set so the next tick lands on the new breakpoint’s begin. Pause — each paused iteration advances env.now by time_step and subtracts it from the offset: time stays frozen and resuming doesn’t skip ahead.
data.6-lifecycle#6. Lifecycle: Action Method Effect Start start_loop(bp) Optionally step to breakpoint bp, apply fixed invariants, start the thread. Pause / resume pause_loop() / resume_loop() Freeze / unfreeze simulated time. Stop stop_loop() Stop the thread and reset everything: first breakpoint, fresh spacecraft and ground station, no overrides, empty TC stack, data proxy back to SLE. Step step_loop(bp) Select a breakpoint and apply its initial states. SpacecraftSim.apply_fixed_updates() runs at start and after each breakpoint change: currently, in OBSW safe mode both transmitters are off. It is not re-applied on later ticks, so safe mode entered mid-pass leaves the transmitters as they were.
data.the-simulation-loop#The simulation loop: What SimOps does each tick, and how simulated time survives pauses and breakpoint jumps. Code: so/core.py, so/spacecraft.py.
